bottom_line: In patients with type 2 diabetes without previous cardiovascular disease, atorvastatin 10 mg daily vs placebo reduced the primary endpoint (hazard ratio 0.63 [0.48–0.83]).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, allocation to atorvastatin 10 mg daily reduced first major cardiovascular events versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.63 [0.48–0.83], p=0.001), with stroke also reduced (0.52 [0.31–0.89]). The mortality result was not statistically significant (0.73 [0.52–1.01], p=0.059), so this document does not license a definite conclusion of reduced all-cause mortality based on CARDS alone.

major_points.text: Multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled trial in the UK and Ireland.
major_points.quote: 2838 patients aged 40–75 years in 132 centres in the UK and Ireland were randomised to placebo (n=1410) or atorvastatin 10 mg daily (n=1428).

major_points.text: Participants had type 2 diabetes with no documented previous cardiovascular disease and LDL-cholesterol ≤4.14 mmol/L.
major_points.quote: Study entrants had no documented previous history of cardiovascular disease, an LDL-cholesterol concentration of 4·14 mmol/L or lower

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was time to first acute CHD event, coronary revascularisation, or stroke; analysis was intention to treat.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoint was time to ﬁrst occurrence of the following: acute coronary heart disease events, coronary revascularisation, or stroke. Analysis was by intention to treat.

major_points.text: Trial was terminated early for efficacy at the second interim analysis.
major_points.quote: The trial was terminated 2 years earlier than expected because the prespeciﬁed early stopping rule for efﬁcacy had been met.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint events were lower with atorvastatin: 127 vs 83; hazard ratio 0.63 (0.48–0.83), p=0.001.
No excess of adverse events was noted in the atorvastatin group.
major_points.quote: No excess of adverse events was noted in the atorvastatin group.

absolute_effects.text: Primary endpoint event rates per 100 person-years: 2.46 placebo vs 1.54 atorvastatin.
absolute_effects.quote: 127 patients allocated placebo (2·46 per 100 person-years at risk) and 83 allocated atorvastatin (1·54 per 100 person-years at risk)

absolute_effects.text: Incidence of major cardiovascular disease events: 24.6 per 1000 person-years placebo vs 15.4 per 1000 person-years atorvastatin.
absolute_effects.quote: Incidence of major cardiovascular disease events was 24·6 per 1000 person-years at risk in the placebo group and 15·4 per 1000 person-years at risk in the atorvastatin group.

absolute_effects.text: Absolute benefit statement: allocation of 1000 patients would avoid 37 first major cardiovascular disease events over 4 years; NNT 27 for 4 years.
absolute_effects.quote: allocation of 1000 patients to atorvastatin 10 mg daily would avoid 37 ﬁrst major cardiovascular disease events over a 4-year follow-up period. 27 patients would need to be treated for 4 years to prevent one event.

absolute_effects.text: First or subsequent major cardiovascular disease events: 31.8 per 1000 person-years placebo vs 19.5 per 1000 person years atorvastatin; 50 fewer events over 4 years per 1000 allocated.
absolute_effects.quote: incidence of ﬁrst or subsequent major cardiovascular disease events was 31·8 per 1000 person-years at risk in the placebo group and 19·5 per 1000 person years at risk in the atorvastatin group.

subgroups.text: Prespecified tests of heterogeneity assessed subgroup differences by age, sex, and baseline lipids.
subgroups.quote: Prespeciﬁed tests of heterogeneity were used to assess whether the effects in particular subgroups (age, sex, and baseline lipids) differed between groups

subgroups.text: No significant heterogeneity of effect for sex or median age at entry.
subgroups.quote: Prespeciﬁed tests for evidence of heterogeneity of effect were not signiﬁcant for sex (p=0·59) or median age at entry (p=0·58).

subgroups.text: No evidence of heterogeneity recorded for baseline systolic blood pressure, retinopathy, albuminuria, smoking status, or HbA1c.
subgroups.quote: No evidence of heterogeneity was recorded for baseline systolic blood pressure (p=0·2), retinopathy (p=0·7), albuminuria (p=0·34), smoking status (p=0·7), or HbA1c (p=0·7).

subgroups.text: Primary endpoint subgroup results by baseline median LDL-cholesterol with heterogeneity p=0.96.

harms.text: Overall frequency of adverse events or serious adverse events did not differ between treatments.
harms.quote: Overall frequency of adverse events or serious adverse events did not differ between treatments.

harms.text: Serious adverse events possibly associated with study drug occurred in 1.1% in each group (19 atorvastatin, 20 placebo).
harms.quote: 1·1% of patients randomised (19 atorvastatin, 20 placebo) had one or more serious adverse events judged by the attending clinician to be possibly associated with study drug.

harms.text: Discontinued study drug due to an adverse event: 145 (10%) placebo vs 122 (9%) atorvastatin.
harms.quote: they discontinued study drug at some point during the trial because of an adverse event (145 [10%] placebo, 122 [9%] atorvastatin).

harms.text: No occurrences of rhabdomyolysis were reported.
harms.quote: No occurrences of rhabdomyolysis were reported.

harms.text: Myalgia noted in 72 patients allocated placebo and 61 allocated atorvastatin.
harms.quote: myalgia was noted in 72 patients allocated placebo and 61 allocated atorvastatin.

harms.text: Alanine transaminase ≥3× upper limit of normal: 14 (1%) placebo vs 17 (1%) atorvastatin.
harms.quote: 14 (1%) individuals allocated placebo and 17 (1%) atorvastatin had at least one increase of alanine transaminase of three or more times the upper limit of normal.

guidelines_referenced.quote: The American Diabetes Association, the Joint European Societies, and the National Cholesterol Education Programme (NCEP) panel
The American Diabetes Association, the Joint European Societies, and the National Cholesterol Education Programme (NCEP) panel
The American Diabetes Association, the Joint European Societies, and the National Cholesterol Education Programme (NCEP) panel

guidelines_referenced.text: NCEP Adult Treatment Panel III guidelines
guidelines_referenced.quote: In July, 2004, the NCEP made a revision of the ATP III guidelines recommending optional target concentrations of LDL-cholesterol

Thus, much of the efﬁcacy and safety proﬁle reported in CARDS relates to levels of starting and achieved LDL-cholesterol below those speciﬁed in the European Societies and American Diabetes Association guidelines.

inclusion_criteria.text: Aged 40–75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at least 6 months before study entry.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Men and women aged 40–75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus (deﬁned with 1985 WHO criteria) diagnosed at least 6 months before study entry

inclusion_criteria.text: Mean serum LDL-cholesterol during baseline visits ≤4.14 mmol/L and serum triglycerides ≤6.78 mmol/L.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Mean serum LDL-cholesterol concentration during baseline visits had to be 4·14 mmol/L or lower and serum triglycerides 6·78 mmol/L or less.

exclusion_criteria.text: Any past history of myocardial infarction, angina, coronary vascular surgery, cerebrovascular accident, or severe peripheral vascular disease (warranting surgery).
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were ineligible if they had any past history of myocardial infarction, angina, coronary vascular surgery, cerebrovascular accident, or severe peripheral vascular disease (deﬁned as warranting surgery).

exclusion_criteria.text: Less than 80% compliance with placebo during the baseline phase.
exclusion_criteria.quote: or if during the baseline phase they had less than 80% compliance with placebo.

analysis_methods.text: Designed for 90% power to detect a one-third reduction in the primary endpoint at p<0.05.
analysis_methods.quote: The study was designed to have 90% power to detect a reduction of a third in the primary endpoint in the atorvastatin 10 mg daily group at a signiﬁcance level of p<0·05.

analysis_methods.text: Planned accrual of 304 primary endpoints to achieve specified power, assuming annual incidence 2.35% in placebo group.
analysis_methods.quote: assuming a cumulative annual incidence of 2·35% for the primary endpoint in the placebo group, a total of 304 primary endpoints needed to accrue.

analysis_methods.text: Main analysis was Cox regression survival analysis comparing hazard rates, yielding hazard ratio.
analysis_methods.quote: The main analysis was a Cox regression survival analysis, comparing the hazard rates for the primary endpoint in the two treatment groups, yielding the hazard ratio

analysis_methods.text: Interim analyses used asymmetric (Peto-Haybittle) rule with prespecified stopping boundaries.
analysis_methods.quote: The interim analyses used an asymmetric (Peto-Haybittle) type rule

analysis_methods.text: Primary endpoint significance threshold p<0.049 to allow for interim analysis effects on type 1 error rate.
analysis_methods.quote: We judged p<0·049 to be signiﬁcant for the primary endpoint analyses because this value allowed for the interim analysis effects on the type 1 error rate.

trial_conduct.text: Ethics approval obtained at each centre after multicentre research ethics committee approval.
trial_conduct.quote: Every centre obtained local research ethics committee approval after approval from the multicentre research ethics committee.

trial_conduct.text: All patients gave fully informed written consent.
trial_conduct.quote: All patients gave fully informed written consent.

trial_conduct.text: Patients seen monthly for first 3 months, then at 6 months and 6-monthly thereafter with safety checks and adverse event recording.
trial_conduct.quote: We saw patients monthly for the ﬁrst 3 months, then at 6 months, and thereafter 6-monthly. At these visits, we checked safety variables, recorded any adverse events

trial_conduct.text: Independent endpoint committee reviewed and classified reported cardiovascular events and deaths.
trial_conduct.quote: An independent endpoint committee reviewed all reported cardiovascular events and deaths and classiﬁed them according to criteria speciﬁed in the endpoint protocol.

trial_conduct.text: Independent data and safety monitoring board undertook interim analyses at 25%, 50%, and 75% of anticipated primary endpoints.
trial_conduct.quote: the independent data and safety monitoring board would undertake an interim analysis when 25%, 50%, and 75% of the total anticipated primary endpoints had accrued.

trial_conduct.text: At second interim analysis, significant difference favored atorvastatin (p<0.001 two-sided) and board recommended termination; announced June 12, 2003.
trial_conduct.quote: At the second interim analysis a signiﬁcant difference was reported in favour of atorvastatin at p<0·001 (two-sided) and so the data and safety monitoring board recommended termination.

funding_declarations.text: Funded by the UK Department of Health, Diabetes UK, and Pfizer.
funding_declarations.quote: was funded by the UK Department of Health, Diabetes UK, and Pﬁzer.

funding_declarations.text: Funding sources had voting member on executive and steering committees; Pfizer staff did site monitoring and data collection/entry; data analysis was done independently by coordinating centre at UCL.
funding_declarations.quote: All three funding sources had a voting member on the executive and steering committees. Site monitoring, data collection, and data entry was done by staff at Pﬁzer UK

funding_declarations.text: Sponsors could comment on manuscript but had no right of veto.
funding_declarations.quote: although the sponsors were allowed to comment on the manuscript they had no right of veto over any of its contents.

funding_declarations.text: Several investigators report consulting/speaking/travel/funding relationships with Pfizer (and others).
funding_declarations.quote: DJB and HMC have served as consultants to, and received travel expenses and payments for speaking at meetings from, Pﬁzer.

criticisms.text: Power to detect differences in subgroup effects or within subgroups was limited, particularly since the trial terminated early.
criticisms.quote: The power to detect small differences in treatment effect between subgroups or to detect signiﬁcance of treatment effect within subgroups is limited, particularly since the trial terminated early.

criticisms.text: Early termination led to fewer deaths than envisaged, reducing power to show a significant reduction in all-cause mortality.
criticisms.quote: The early termination of the trial meant that fewer deaths were observed than originally envisaged, reducing the power of the trial to show a signiﬁcant reduction in all-cause mortality.

criticisms.text: One important issue CARDS cannot address is whether higher-dose atorvastatin or addition of other drugs would achieve greater relative risk reduction.
criticisms.quote: One of the important issues that CARDS cannot address is whether a higher dose of atorvastatin or addition of other drugs such as a ﬁbrate or a selective cholesterol absorption inhibitor
